html:
A rubber company formed after the American tyre maker Firestone signed a 99-year lease in 1926 for up to a million acres of Liberian land, at six cents an acre.

Its plantation at Harbel became for a time the largest rubber plantation in the world, and the deal came with a loan to the Liberian government that gave American advisers control over its finances. Rubber became Liberia's main export, and Firestone the largest employer, with workers' camps, schools and a hospital, and long labour disputes. During the civil war the plantation was fought over and used by Charles Taylor. See also rubber.
